place: Murshidabad and Malda districts (with Uttar and Dakshin Dinajpur), West Bengal

items.claim: When the final roll was published on 28 February 2026, about 11 lakh of the 60,06,675 cases under adjudication were in Murshidabad and about 8 lakh in Malda, close to a third of the state's total, with 4.8 lakh in Uttar Dinajpur, according to the CEO's data.
items.quote: There are 60,06,675 cases under adjudication in the final roll published on February 28, 2026. ... including 11 lakh in Murshidabad and eight lakh in Malda. In fact, these two districts bordering Bangladesh have almost one third of cases under adjudication. There are 4.8 lakh cases under adjudication in Uttar Dinajpur
items.outlet: The Hindu (from data shared by the West Bengal CEO)
items.note: The article's headline and framing describe the districts by religion; that framing is not used here. Quote omits the religious descriptor at the start of the second sentence (ellipsis).

items.claim: The Election Commission's district table of adjudication outcomes shows Murshidabad with 11,01,145 cases, 6,33,671 found eligible and 4,55,137 found not eligible; Malda 8,28,127, 5,88,657 and 2,39,375; Uttar Dinajpur 4,80,341, 3,03,261 and 1,76,972; Dakshin Dinajpur 1,32,258, 55,490 and 76,768.
items.outlet: The Indian Express (ECI district-wise data reproduced)
items.note: Columns: action to be taken, found eligible, found not eligible. State totals 60,06,675 / 32,68,119 / 27,16,393 match the site's raw/adjudication_state.csv. Shares not eligible: Malda 28.9%, Murshidabad 41.3%, Uttar Dinajpur 36.8%, Dakshin Dinajpur 58.0% (the paper prints 28.91, 41.33, 36.84). The ECI's own release was not found online; this is the ECI table as the paper printed it. In Murshidabad 'action taken' (10,88,808) was below 'action to be taken'. The article describes the districts by religion; not used.

items.claim: Hindustan Times, citing ECI data, reported Murshidabad had the most adjudication deletions of any district (4,55,137) and Malda the third most (2,39,375), while Dakshin Dinajpur had among the highest rejection rates at 58.1%.
items.quote: In terms of absolute numbers, the districts recording the highest number of deletions were Murshidabad (455,137), North 24 Parganas (325,666), Malda (239,375), South 24 Parganas (222,929) and Purba Bardhaman (209,805). ... Kolkata North recorded a rejection rate of 63.9%, followed by Dakshin Dinajpur (58.1%)
items.note: Updated 10 April 2026. Same article quotes a senior ECI official in Kolkata: of about six million cases 'around 45% were found ineligible'. Party statements in the article (TMC chief, BJP leaders) are not used. Religious descriptors of districts in the article are not used.

items.claim: By constituency, Samserganj (Murshidabad) lost 74,775 of 1,08,400 names under adjudication and Lalgola 55,420 of 99,082, and in Malda more than 37,000 of 79,683 under adjudication in Mothabari were removed, according to collated Election Commission data.
items.quote: The figures for Murshidabad - 74,775 deletions out of 1,08,400 names that were under adjudication in Shamsherganj, followed by 55,420 out of 99,082 in Lalgola ... More than 37,000 names out of 79,683 under adjudication in Mothabari were struck off the rolls.
items.note: The paper says the figures are 'based on collated Election Commission data released on Thursday'. Its headline and first sentence describe areas by religion and community; not used. The article also links Samserganj to earlier unrest; not used. Civic Research Group's later count for Samserganj is 71,985 (mm-10); the difference is unexplained.

items.claim: At booth level, The Indian Express found 327 of 444 names under adjudication deleted in booth 3 and 422 of 527 in booth 4 of a village in Sujapur (Malda), and 291 of 591 and 207 of 361 in booths 111 and 112 of Suti (Murshidabad).
items.quote: In the Bahadurpur Kabirajtala village in the Kaliachak block, under the Sujapur assembly seat in Malda, 327 names were deleted from the 444 under adjudication in booth 3. In booth 4, 422 names were deleted from the 527 under adjudication. ... In booth 111, a total of 291 names were deleted from the 591 under adjudication. In booth number 112, 207 names were deleted from the 361 under adjudication.
items.note: Same article: Malda 8.28 lakh and Murshidabad 11 lakh adjudication cases; 705 judicial officers; tribunals not yet set up at the time. It names many individual voters (doctors, a police officer, a BSF jawan, lawyers, a panchayat member); none named here. A panchayat member's allegation of deliberate deletion is not used.

items.claim: On 1 April 2026 voters removed after adjudication surrounded seven judicial officers at the BDO office in Kaliachak block, Malda, and protesters blocked National Highway 12; Malda had about 8.30 lakh adjudicated electors against a district electorate of 29.86 lakh.
items.quote: Several voters who were removed from the electoral rolls of West Bengal after the controversial Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise have gheraoed seven judicial officers (JOs) in Malda district's Kaliachak block. ... Malda district has recorded more than 18,000 dead and duplicate voters, while the number of adjudicated electors stands at around 8.30 lakh—a significant figure compared to the total electorate of 29.86 lakh in the district.
items.note: Sources in the CEO's office told the paper the SP and ADM reached the spot around 11 pm. District administration sources said protests intensified after names were missing from the supplementary lists. The article's description of the block by religion is not used.

items.claim: The Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of the gherao of seven judicial officers at the BDO office in Kaliachowk, Maldah, ordered central forces wherever judicial officers were adjudicating SIR claims, asked the Maldah DM and SP to show cause, and directed the Commission to hand the inquiry to the CBI or the NIA.
items.quote: seven judicial officers, including three women, were gheraoed by anti-social elements at the BDO office in the Kaliachowk area of Maldah District. ... (vii) Additionally, the Chief Secretary, the Director General of Police, the District Magistrate, Maldah and the Superintendent of Police, Maldah are also directed to show cause ... (viii) We also direct the ECI to entrust the inquiry/ investigation into yesterday’s incident to an independent agency, such as the Central Bureau of Investigation or the National Investigation Agency.
items.outlet: Supreme Court of India, Suo Motu W.P.(C) No. 3 of 2026, order of 2 April 2026
items.note: Already in the site's disputes research as court-19; re-read here. The order also limits gatherings at adjudication premises to five persons and notes the matter is under consideration in W.P.(C) No. 1089/2025.

items.claim: The NIA, which took over the Mothabari case on the Supreme Court's direction, had arrested 68 people by 26 May 2026.
items.quote: With this, 68 people have been arrested in the case so far, they added. ... The NIA took over the investigation into the case following the direction of the Supreme Court.
items.note: The article names party candidates and leaders among those arrested; not repeated here. It describes the crowd as 'protesting the deletion of names from voters' lists'. No charge sheet found.

items.claim: Visiting Beldanga in Murshidabad, West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told a resident asking for deleted names to be restored that the deletions had been made by judicial officers under the Supreme Court's directions; the paper put Murshidabad's total deletions at 7,48,959.
items.quote: “With directives of the Supreme Court, judicial officers had handled the under-adjudication cases. The deletions of names have been done by the judicial officers. Let me see what I can do.” ... Out of 11,01,145 adjudicated voters, 4,55,137 have been marked ineligible, and a total of 7,48,959 names have been deleted from the district’s rolls.
items.note: Official statement by the CEO (by office). 7,48,959 would be 4,55,137 adjudication deletions plus 2,93,822 earlier deletions (UNI's figure for names removed before adjudication; UNI post seen as snippet only). Article names several villagers and quotes a resident's religious framing; neither used.

items.claim: An analysis of Commission portal records by the Civic Research Group found 3,72,240 appeals recorded against adjudication deletions in Murshidabad, with decisions recorded in only 275 as of 28 September 2026; in Samserganj 62,630 appeals were pending.
items.quote: Of the 3,72,240 appeals recorded in Murshidabad, 260 were approved and 15 rejected. This means that 3,71,965 appeals remained pending in the CRG dataset.
items.outlet: Muslim Mirror (also Maktoob Media, same date), reporting Civic Research Group's analysis
items.note: Secondary analysis of the ECI appeal portal, not an official count; CRG cautions about incomplete data and offline appeals not yet uploaded ('not applied' 13,216). CRG's Murshidabad adjudication deletions are 4,44,337 against the ECI table's 4,55,137 (mm-02); the gap is unexplained. Maktoob: https://maktoobmedia.com/post?id=116638&slug=in-bengals-murshidabad-372-lakh-deleted-voters-appealed-only-275-decisions-recorded. Statewide, the ECI told the Supreme Court on 18 September that 38.31 lakh appeals had been filed and 1.26 lakh disposed of by 10 September (reported by Sabrang, mm-11).

items.claim: The Election Commission's own claims-and-objections data, filed in a counter-affidavit and analysed by The Wire, show that in Murshidabad 10.58% of Form 6 inclusion applications led to additions against 87.71% of Form 7 deletion requests leading to deletions, and in Uttar Dinajpur 8.16% against 96.11%; in Chopra 948 of 954 Form 7 requests ended in deletion while 28 of 28,701 Form 6 applications led to additions.
items.quote: Uttar Dinajpur recorded additions from 8.16% of inclusion applications and deletions from 96.11% of deletion requests. The corresponding figures were 8.21% and 98.59% in Jalpaiguri, and 10.58% and 87.71% in Murshidabad. ... Chopra recorded 948 deletions from 954 requests, while only 28 names were added from 28,701 inclusion applications.
items.outlet: SabrangIndia (summarising The Wire's analysis of ECI counter-affidavit annexures R/1 and R/2)
items.note: Covers claims and objections from 17 Dec 2025 to 7 Aug 2026. Malda's and Dakshin Dinajpur's rates are not given in the text read. The Wire's original and the affidavit itself were not read; mark as a second-hand account until the affidavit annexures are found. Chopra and Islampur are in Uttar Dinajpur.

items.claim: Families of four migrant workers from Samserganj, whose names were deleted in the SIR and whose tribunal appeals were pending, petitioned the Calcutta High Court over their detention in Chhattisgarh; the court asked what the appellate tribunal would decide if other authorities were already taking a view.
items.quote: The family members of these four persons have now filed a petition at the Calcutta High Court, pleading to direct the Chhattisgarh government to release the detainees. The petitioners said that they were detained even while their appeals against the deletion of their names from the electoral rolls are pending before the tribunal.
items.note: SENSITIVE. The case concerns detention over nationality questions; under the site's rules nothing may say or imply anything about any person's citizenship. If used at all, use only as a court-process item (petition pending while tribunal appeals undecided). The article names the four men; not named here. It dates the first hearing 'Monday (September 5, 2026)', but 5 September 2026 was a Saturday; the date is uncertain. No order text found. Read from the full text returned by search.

not_found: No district-level press note from the DEO Murshidabad or DEO Malda giving their own adjudication, Form 6, Form 7 or hearing figures was found; district figures here come from the ECI table as printed by The Indian Express (mm-02) and from press.
The ECI's own published release or PDF of the district-wise adjudication table (April 2026) was not found online; only the newspaper reproductions.

No district or constituency split of tribunal (appeal) outcomes from an official source; the only district appeal figures are Civic Research Group's portal analysis (mm-10). Malda, Uttar Dinajpur and Dakshin Dinajpur appeal figures were not found.
Form 6 / Form 7 rates for Malda and Dakshin Dinajpur were not in the text read (mm-11); the ECI counter-affidavit annexures R/1 and R/2 themselves were not found.
No Calcutta High Court order specific to adjudication in Murshidabad or Malda was found; the only Murshidabad HC matter found is the detention petition (mm-12), which the site's rules may exclude.
No charge sheet or NIA statement on the Mothabari case beyond press arrest counts (mm-08).
No official figure for how many in Murshidabad or Malda were restored after appeal.
Reasons for adjudication outcomes by district (name mismatch, age gap, more than six children linked to a parent, etc.) were not published by district; only state-level descriptions in press.
Press religion or community splits of the adjudicated were seen in several sources (The Hindu, HT, TOI, IE headlines) and deliberately not used.
No figure was found reconciling CRG's Murshidabad deletion count (4,44,337) with the ECI table (4,55,137), or TOI's Samserganj figure (74,775) with CRG's (71,985).
